opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access; their role does not own Source Code so admin is not applicable. Requested write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E005 shows contractor with basic security training (note: this conflicts with HR's full-time classification). Contractors with basic training max out at read access; requested write is above policy, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: Security's record (looked up in its own database) classifies Casey Wu (E005) as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read access; the requested write is above the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. Note: HR's record lists the employee as full-time, creating a conflict, but the security note specifically identifies the contractor classification and basic training, and granting read stays within policy bounds.

2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time: requested write is within policy → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read → grant read (requested write is above max).
